headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared server datastore and filesystem; no documented pairwise isolation between Flowise and plano.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the filesystem and uses browser and HTTP tools; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and config files. Flowise’s shared server datastore plus file surfaces create a plausible path for plano-originated content to be re-ingested as instructions. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented for the pair, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Flowise ingests plano-generated text from shared files or datastore entries as trusted instructions
IF plano outputs attacker-controlled content that Flowise later parses as tool directives
mitigations: Disable shared datastore access between the two systems for untrusted content
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Route inter-agent text through a sanitizer that strips instructions
Review Flowise flows for file-ingest nodes before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, while plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive chatflow content can leak into plano telemetry or logs. The profiles do not document a hard isolation boundary, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or datastore
IF Flowise uploads chatflow files that plano also logs or traces
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points
Redact secrets before logs are emitted
Disable verbose tracing for shared data classes
Audit config.yaml for accidental secret references
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress; plano has broad network egress and an out-of-process dataplane. Even without explicit modify_git_state overlap, both can mutate shared external resources or files if deployed together. Because the shared-state model is documented only for Flowise and not coordinated with plano, conflict risk is real but not high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared datastore
IF both are configured to update the same external API or backend resource
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Use per-agent credentials for external APIs
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Turn off shared mutable state where possible
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder, so its outputs can become downstream inputs; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint that may be consumed as authoritative text. If Flowise-generated content is routed into plano without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or routing decisions. The pair lacks documented verification controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Flowise output is forwarded into plano without a validation step
IF plano treats Flowise-produced text as authoritative routing or policy input
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Require schema validation on inter-agent messages
Log and diff outputs before acting on them
Limit plano to read-only advisory mode
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection paths

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials while plano handles logs, traces, and metrics. A compliance issue only appears if regulated data is routed into plano’s telemetry or if Flowise secrets are stored in shared logs. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in plano logs, traces, or metrics
IF Flowise secrets are written into shared operational logs
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from telemetry
Rotate any exposed credentials
Set log retention to the minimum practical period
Review data-processing notices for both systems
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries
